pr_title: Fix Lutron Caseta devices loading when missing serials

## Proposed change
**This PR fixes the issue that some Lutron Caseta devices won't load because they don't have serials.
For an example, Lutron Caseta aggregates sensors in the same room into a single sensor entity, in this case, the single sensor entity won't have a serial.**
The issue is https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/37449

pr_comments:
Fixing the lint issue.

EDIT: fixed

Seem a bit odd, since the same class contains this:

```py
    @property
    def serial(self):	    def serial(self):
        """Return the serial number of the device."""	        """Return the serial number of the device."""
        return self._device["serial"]	        return self._device["serial"]
```

As that property is used for the unique_id, it would cause a stack trace to be thrown, as shown in the linked issue #37449.

So my initial hunch, is that this doesn't fix the issue (or a least just partly).

> Seem a bit odd, since the same class contains this:
> 
> ```python
>     @property
>     def serial(self):	    def serial(self):
>         """Return the serial number of the device."""	        """Return the serial number of the device."""
>         return self._device["serial"]	        return self._device["serial"]
> ```
> 
> As that property is used for the unique_id, it would cause a stack trace to be thrown, as shown in the linked issue #37449.
> 
> So my initial hunch, is that this doesn't fix the issue (or a least just partly).

The stack trace shown in #37449 was NOT caused by the using of `unique_id`, it was caused by getting `device_info`.

`File "/usr/src/homeassistant/homeassistant/helpers/entity_platform.py", line 343, in _async_add_entity
device_info = entity.device_info`

This PR fixes exact the stack trace in issue #37449 .

It is indeed interesting that `unique_id` is using serial which could be a problem. But it is not the issue, the only thing I've touched (in previous PR https://github.com/home-assistant/core/issues/37449 and this PR) is the `device_info`.

Let me take a look how `unique_id` is used, to make sure it won't cause another issue.

Based on the developer documentation, `unique_id` is indeed used for entity registry. But what's wired is that this was added 8 months ago (https://github.com/home-assistant/core/pull/28886), and nobody has ever reported any issues.

I'm in contact with someone who has Caseta sensors, trying to figure out what `unique_id` has been registered in the entity_registry.
My unique_id for my sensor is "occupancygroup_16", which lines up with the LEAP device ID.  I can check my friend’s HA instance if you guys want - he has 5 sensors.

@jsb5151 @frenck 

I found out the reason that the usage of `self.serial` in `unique_id` hasn't been causing issue:

The only devices that won't have serial are sensors, and in `binary_sensor.py` subclass, `unique_id` is overwritten with `occupancygroup_{self.device_id}` 

https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/a00aa6740e87d16999bbf19ac22acaa4d915de71/homeassistant/components/lutron_caseta/binary_sensor.py#L57

With that being said, only `device_info`'s usage of `serial` has been causing issues and this PR fixes it. Hope this makes sense.

Fixing the lint issues.

Update: Fixed and testing now.

Leaving a quick update on the issue (thanks to **plomdawg@discord**'s help):

1. the issue is straightforward: motion sensors don't have a `serial`
2. reason being that Caseta combines sensors (no matter how many) in the same room into a single entity therefore the entity doesn't have a `serial`
3. even there is only one motion sensor in a single room, the entity still doesn't have a `serial`.

an example of a sensor:  
`{'occupancy_group_id': '3', 'name': 'The Bathroom Occupancy', 'status': 'Unoccupied'}`

IMO if the sensor entities in Caseta are all 'combined entity', they technically don't belong to any physical devices, so I think we should NOT create devices for Caseta sensor entities.

But that'd make it impossible to assign the Caseta sensor entities to areas. That shouldn't be a big deal since people have been using them this way since the beginning, even though I personally would like to be able to assign them to areas.

Could you generate a serial based in the group id and name? So that you can assign the "device" to an area and always generate the same "serial".
If you guys need testing I can help too.

I love the caseta sensors, they are so sensitive, I also have z-wave PIR sensors but not as good as the caseta, so I don't use them. The only problem is that you can't program a schedule for the sensors in the app, so it turns on the light even during the day. I use HA-NodeRed to turn them on only at night.
You might be right that you can't use the individual sensors, because they are not even exposed on the telnet interface and you can't use any sensor that way.
Any update on this?  I received my sensor and am testing this using another control system and it works fine.  I can assist with debugging on the LEAP interface if required.

review_comments:
We should `return None` here explicitly even though pylint doesn't understand that. We can disable pylint locally.
```suggestion
    @property
    def device_info(self):
        """Return the device info.

        Sensor entities are aggregated from one or more physical
        sensors by each room. Therefore, there shouldn't be devices
        related to any sensor entities.
        """
        return None  # pylint: disable=useless-return
```
